statements.t: The Company expects to use cash on hand and proceeds from the sale of its remaining properties to pay operating expenses, satisfy obligations owing to Curbline, manage overall liquidity levels, make distributions to shareholders and establish a reserve fund to satisfy projected expenses and known and unknown claims that might arise during the anticipated wind-up of its business.

The Company expects that rental income and net income will continue to decrease in future periods as compared to corresponding prior year periods as a result of significant disposition activity and declining property revenues.
The Company requires capital to fund its operating expenses, obligations owing to Curbline and the anticipated wind-up of its business.

The Company does not maintain a revolving credit facility and therefore plans to closely monitor and conservatively manage its liquidity and cash position as it pursues the sale of its remaining properties, manages the wind-up of its business and returns capital to shareholders.

As of September 30, 2026, the Company anticipates that it has approximately $6.1 million to be incurred to complete redevelopment projects at properties owned by Curbline pursuant to the terms of the Separation and Distribution Agreement.
The Company also expects to pay a special cash dividend of $3.00 per share ($158.1 million in the aggregate) to common shareholders on November 5, 2026.

As the Company pursues the sale of its remaining properties, there are many factors that may affect the timing and amount of additional distributions to shareholders, including, among other things, the timing and amount received from the disposition of the remaining assets, ongoing obligations owed to Curbline under the Shared Services Agreement, and projected expenses and known and unknown claims that might…
In the event the Company is able to sell its remaining assets, the Company expects to subsequently file articles of dissolution with the Secretary of State of the State of Ohio.

Therefore, the Company expects to conservatively manage its cash position and establish a reserve fund with a portion of its current cash balance and proceeds from its final sales in order to satisfy and discharge expenses projected to be incurred, and any unknown or contingent claims, debts or obligations which might arise, during the five-year period subsequent to the filing of the articles of dissolution.
The Company may also become the subject of litigation (which may not be covered by insurance) or other claims that are not currently known or expected.

Prior to the anticipated termination of the Shared Services Agreement on October 1, 2027, the Company’s general and administrative expenses will remain elevated as a result of contractual obligations and services owing to Curbline Properties thereunder.

Upon or shortly following termination of the Shared Services Agreement, in an effort to reduce its operating expenses and maximize liquidating distributions to shareholders, the Company expects to terminate most or all of its remaining employees and engage an external advisor to administer the remainder of the five-year statutory wind-up period.

Throughout the administration of the Company’s anticipated wind-up and dissolution, the Company will be required to continue to comply with the applicable reporting requirements of the Exchange Act, even if compliance with these reporting requirements is economically burdensome.

In order to curtail expenses, sometime during the months following filing articles of dissolution, the Company expects to avail itself of relief provided by the Securities and Exchange Commission that allows certain liquidating REITs to end most of their Exchange Act reporting while winding up their businesses.

Additionally, the Company anticipates that as part of such process the over-the-counter market would no longer quote prices for the Company’s common shares and The Depository Trust Company would cease to permit transfers of the Company’s common shares among its participants.
The Company expects these developments would cause brokers to significantly restrict future trading in the shares.
As a result, the Company expects that liquidity in its shares would be significantly curtailed.

The Company does not expect to have REIT taxable income in 2026 or 2027 and expects that continued maintenance of its REIT qualification will become impractical and increasingly difficult due to the sale of substantially all of its real estate investments.
Therefore, the Company may elect to surrender its REIT status in connection with the sale of its remaining assets and the anticipated wind-up of its operations.
Following the de-listing of its shares from the NYSE, the Company expects that its shares will trade in the over-the-counter market and be quoted on the OTCID Basic Market.

The Company may be unable to accurately project costs and expenses relating to its disposition and wind-up strategy and may encounter exposure to unexpected claims, liabilities or costs in connection therewith;
The Company provided notice to the New York Stock Exchange of its plan to voluntarily de-list its common shares prior to the commencement of trading on December 4, 2026.
Following the de-listing, the Company expects that its common shares will trade in the over-the-counter market and be quoted on the OTCID Basic Market.
Based upon preliminary analysis to date, the Company does not expect to have REIT taxable income in 2026 and estimates that 100% of its 2026 distributions will be return of capital.
